title: 2023 HMMT November Guts Problem 12
statement: A jar contains 97 marbles that are either red, green, or blue. Neil draws two marbles from the jar without replacement and notes that the probability that they would be the same color is \(\frac{5}{12}\). After Neil puts his marbles back, Jerry draws two marbles from the jar with replacement. Compute the probability that the marbles that Jerry draws are the same color.

solutions.text:
Let there be \(a, b\), and \(c\) marbles of each type. We know \(a+b+c=97\) and

\[\frac{a^{2}-a+b^{2}-b+c^{2}-c}{97 \cdot 96}=\frac{a^{2}+b^{2}+c^{2}-97}{97 \cdot 96}=\frac{5}{12}=\frac{40}{96}\]

This means \(a^{2}+b^{2}+c^{2}=41 \cdot 97\). Then the probability Bob's marbles are the same color is

\[\frac{a^{2}+b^{2}+c^{2}}{97^{2}}=\frac{41}{97}\]

Remark. A triple \((a, b, c)\) that works is \((12,32,53)\).
